coverage: Read full native PCB, relevant schematic sources, project rules, and supplied DRC/ERC/netlist/geometry records.
Reproduced configured DRC: 142 violations, 114 parity issues, zero unconnected items; all 13 error-level results are excluded.
Independently compared 659 schematic pin-to-net assignments against PCB pads: no missing pins or net-name mismatches.
Measured connector hole annuli and exported separate plated/unplated drill files.
Inspected saved ground copper and routed connections at all three starved thermals.
Checked CAN2 termination population, connectivity, and ideal resistance calculations; sampled power, heater, and ground routing geometry.

findings.condition: Five unnumbered J1 holes are declared plated through holes with copper diameter equal to drill diameter: three at 4.0 mm and two at 2.2 mm.

evidence.locator: Lines 1564–1573; T10 and T12 emit all five holes as plated

findings.mechanism: Annulus = (pad diameter − drill diameter)/2 = 0 mm, below the configured 0.1 mm minimum. Drill export preserves their plated classification.
findings.reasoning: This is a reproducible native padstack/rule violation, despite its exclusion. Whether these were intended as unplated locating holes remains unresolved; the evidence does not establish connector fit failure or fabrication rejection.
findings.title: Five plated J1 holes have zero annular copper

findings.condition: Saved F.Cu ground reliefs at C15.2, U7.4, and C14.2 each resolve one spoke against a configured minimum of two.

evidence.locator: GND zone UUID bc540b8b-3ffa-4b00-b211-3a91191a1f6d, line 69477 onward; saved filled polygons
thermal_pads: pad coordinates, connected 0.25 mm traces, and nearby ground vias

findings.mechanism: The saved zone connections do not satisfy the native minimum spoke count; exclusions suppress disposition without changing copper.
findings.reasoning: Independent DRC reproduces all three violations. Each pad also has a routed ground connection toward a nearby via, so these findings establish a geometric rule violation, not an open ground or demonstrated thermal failure.
findings.title: Three saved ground reliefs violate the spoke minimum

findings.condition: Both carrier CAN2 termination options, R36 and R37, are 120 ohms but DNP and excluded from assembly outputs.

evidence.locator: Lines 2665–2675; resistor UUID d69380f9-5487-4782-9ce9-0690df62e543; R36/R37 instances
R36 at lines 14742–14810; R37 at lines 18665–18733; DNP attributes
nets /CAN2+ and /CAN2-; components R36 and R37

findings.location: Internal dual-wideband CAN2 network, R36/R37 and J2.73/J2.74
findings.mechanism: The saved carrier population contributes no resistive termination. Host-module or harness termination therefore determines the assembled bus loading.
findings.reasoning: The native population is clear, but host/harness termination and electrical behavior are unverified. Ideal carrier-only alternatives are 120 ohms with one resistor and 60 ohms with both. Continuity checks cannot establish appropriate loading or waveform quality, so a communication failure is not asserted.
findings.title: Internal CAN2 termination remains unestablished

limitations: Saved copper only; no refill or candidate modification. Commands, versions, configuration differences, assumptions, and outcomes are recorded in review-work/physical/experiments/review-notes.md.
No hardware resistance, CAN traffic, waveform, cable, rise-time, bus-rate, or host-module population testing.
No component pinout audit, 3D fit, module standoff clearance, fabrication-tolerance qualification, or manufacturing approval.
No ampacity, simultaneous-load, fuse-coordination, thermal, automotive-transient, ignition-energy, wideband-stability, or EMC qualification; widths and via counts do not establish these.
Ignored courtyard checks and the configured zero copper-edge minimum limit mechanical and clearance coverage. Integrated FOME-MC and the separate original as-received checkout were not reviewed.
